question: A network engineer must create an EEM script that saves a copy of the running configuration on bootflash and writes a message to syslog when a user saves the configuration to a Cisco Nexus Series switch. Which configuration set should be applied to complete this task?
options:
event manager applet local-backup
  event cli match "copy running-config startup-config"
  action 1 cli copy running-config bootflash:/current_config.txt
  action 2 syslog msg Configuration saved and copied to bootflash

event manager applet local-backup
  event cli match "copy running-config startup-config"
  action 1 cli copy running-config bootflash:/current_config.txt
  action 2 syslog msg Configuration saved and copied to bootflash
  action 3 event-default

event manager applet local-backup
  event cli match "write memory"
  action 1 cli copy running-config bootflash:/current_config.txt
  action 2 snmp-trap strdata "Configuration saved and copied to bootflash"

event manager applet local-backup
  event cli match "write memory"
  action 1 cli copy running-config bootflash:/current_config.txt
  action 2 syslog msg Configuration saved and copied to bootflash
  action 3 event-default
theory: The applet must match the command engineers actually type today — 'copy running-config startup-config' — not the legacy 'write memory' alias, so the event statement triggers correctly. And because the policy matches a CLI command, it must end with 'action ... event-default' so the original command is still allowed to run after the backup-and-syslog actions execute; without event-default the save would be silently blocked, just as in the EEM CLI-match behavior described in the book. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 16 — Automation and Scripting Tools)
